title: nullroute module specification
description: Every module in packages/core, and every security-relevant module elsewhere, has a sibling *.spec.yaml conforming to this schema. `make verify` asserts that every exported symbol is covered by some spec and that every declared invariant names a test that exists and passed. A spec is not documentation: the device refuses to boot if code, specs, and tests disagree.

id.description: Stable dotted identifier, e.g. core.entropy.combiner. Referenced by commit messages and by other specs.

version.description: Bumped when the specified behaviour changes in a way that would break a third-party reimplementation.

assurance_tier.description: critical: runs near key material (packages/core, signing paths in packages/daemon). standard: the wallet layer, where invariants are about correctness and clarity rather than key safety. experimental: not permitted to claim status `verified`.

status.description: draft: the spec exists, the code may not. implemented: code and tests exist and pass. verified: a human has reviewed the algorithm against its references. Only a maintainer sets `verified`.

purpose.description: What this module is for, and the property that makes it worth having. Not a restatement of the title.

covers.description: Exported symbols this spec accounts for. `make verify` fails if any export of packages/core is not covered by some spec.

items.description: Format: <repo-relative POSIX path>::<Symbol>, optionally <Class>#<method>. `::` is used because neither a POSIX path nor a JS identifier can contain it.

algorithm.description: The construction, precisely enough that a third party could reimplement it and get byte-identical results. Required at the `critical` tier.

invariants.description: Testable assertions. Each must bind to at least one test that exists and passed.

threats.description: Threat identifiers from docs/THREAT-MODEL.md that this module mitigates. The schema only checks the shape; verify checks that the ids resolve.

vectors.description: Official test vector files this module must pass, pinned by content hash so a vector file cannot be edited to make a failing implementation pass.

differential.description: Cross-implementation agreement. Required at the `critical` tier for anything producing a value another implementation can also compute.

security_notes.description: What this module does NOT protect against, and under what assumption it is safe. Overclaiming here is a defect.

references.description: RFCs, BIPs, and papers the algorithm follows.

allOf.$comment: The critical tier carries the real burden. A module that runs near key material must state its algorithm precisely enough to reimplement, must say what it does not defend against, and must cite what it follows.
An experimental module may not claim to be verified. Otherwise `verified` would mean nothing.

constraints.description: Bounds a reimplementation must honour, e.g. "exactly 32 bytes" or "1..8 sources".

id.description: e.g. INV-ENT-1 or INV-BIP39-1. Unique across the repository; verify enforces uniqueness.

statement.description: A falsifiable assertion. If you cannot imagine the test that fails, it is not an invariant.

tests.description: Test selectors. Each MUST resolve to exactly one test that ran and passed. Zero matches and multiple matches are both hard failures, because a duplicate test title would otherwise let a passing test stand in for a failing one.

items.description: Format: <path>.test.ts::<segment>[ > <segment>]*, matched as a suffix of the test's [...ancestorTitles, title].

sha256.description: Content hash of the vector file. Pinned so a vector cannot be edited to make a failing implementation pass.

oracle.description: The independent implementation checked against, e.g. bitcoinjs-lib.

min_cases.description: Minimum number of cases the differential suite must exercise.
